text.en: Spools of plastic filament, the raw material for 3D printers. The printer melts the filament in a heated nozzle and lays it down layer by layer to build the part.
Filament is fed from a spool through a heated extruder head and deposited layer by layer
Thermoplastics such as PLA, ABS, PETG, PET, HIPS, TPU and nylon
Plant-based polyester, low warping and good detail, but softens and deforms above about 60 °C
A stereo microscope is an optical microscope for low-magnification observation, typically using light reflected from the surface of the object rather than transmitted through it.
Two separate optical paths give each eye a slightly different viewing angle, which produces a three-dimensional view of the object.
Optimal working distances range from roughly 150 to 400 mm, which leaves space between the lens and the object.

Stereo microscopes are widely used in manufacturing for manufacture, inspection and quality control, including circuit board manufacture or inspection. Zoom models change magnification continuously across a set range.

title.en: Power supplies, oscilloscope and hot-air tools

text.en: In constant voltage mode the supply delivers the same voltage regardless of the attached load; the current you set is a maximum (current limit), not the current that flows.

source.title: Understanding constant voltage and constant current, Rohde & Schwarz

text.en: An oscilloscope graphs an electrical signal as it varies over time; analog scopes draw the input with an electron beam, digital scopes sample it.

source.title: How to Use an Oscilloscope, SparkFun Learn

text.en: A hot-air station heats quickly and evenly to reflow solder so a component can be attached to or removed from a circuit board; the air is delivered through a hose, which makes it possible to rework surface-mount parts.
A multimeter is a measuring instrument that can measure several electrical properties; a typical one measures voltage, resistance and current.
A soldering iron supplies heat to melt solder so it can flow into the joint between two workpieces.
A soldering station has temperature control that the user can adjust, and it is most commonly used for soldering electronic components.
A pen plotter draws vector artwork by moving a real pen across paper, producing continuous lines rather than printed dots.
A machine that produces vector graphics drawings by drawing lines on paper with a pen
Moves a pen or other instrument across the surface of the paper
Draws continuous lines, unlike inkjet and laser printers that build images from a fine matrix of dots
Can draw complex line art including text, but slowly because of the mechanical movement of the pen

text.en: Electrical Safety First advises checking that lights are not damaged or broken and have no loose wires before use, and switching them off and unplugging them before going to bed or going out. Whether this tree has lights was not verified.

A computer-controlled cutter that moves a small blade along a design drawn on a computer, cutting shapes out of a roll or sheet of vinyl. Typical uses are decals, lettering for signs and iron-on designs for clothing.
A vector design is sent from a computer, and the computer moves a small knife over vinyl fed from a roll.
After cutting, the unwanted pieces are removed from the backing (weeding), leaving only the design.
It cuts shapes from solid-colour material, so photographs and colour gradients cannot be reproduced with a cutter alone.
For clothing, the design is cut as a mirror image in heat transfer vinyl, weeded, then applied with a heat press or an iron.

A heat press: a machine that presses a hot plate onto an item for a set time, using heat and pressure to bond a design onto it. Its typical use is pressing cut iron-on vinyl onto T-shirts, bags and other fabric.
Imprints a design onto an item such as a T-shirt by applying heat and pressure for a preset time.
Applying heat transfer vinyl and sublimation transfers to fabric; specially designed presses can also decorate mugs, plates and caps.
Common designs are clamshell (top plate opens like a shell), swing-away (top plate swings aside) and draw (bottom plate pulls out like a drawer).
Siser EasyWeed heat transfer vinyl is made for cotton, polyester and blends; its clear carrier sheet is peeled away after pressing.

source.title: The basics and benefits of Siser EasyWeed heat transfer vinyl, Siser

text.en: Plywood is made from thin layers (plies) of wood veneer stacked and glued together, with each layer's grain usually perpendicular to its neighbours (cross-graining).

Medium-density fibreboard is an engineered wood made by breaking hardwood or softwood residuals down into wood fibre, combining it with wax and a resin binder, and forming it into panels under high temperature and pressure.
A metric screw is named by the letter M followed by its nominal diameter in mm, for example M8 is an 8 mm thread. The pitch can be added after it, as in M8x1.25.
When the pitch is the normal coarse pitch listed in ISO 261 or ISO 262, it can be left out of the name, so a plain M8 means the standard coarse thread.

Heat-set inserts are stock parts that add threads to a thermoplastic part. The insert is heated with a soldering iron (ideally a non-tapered installation tip) and pushed into an undersized hole; the softened plastic re-solidifies around the insert's knurled feature and holds it in place.

source.title: Threading 3D printed parts: how to use heat-set inserts, Hackaday

text.en: A standard M3 heat-set insert is typically 5.0 mm wide and 4.0 mm tall; a printed hole of about 4.6 to 4.8 mm works well for it.

source.title: Threaded inserts for 3D prints: the complete guide, cre8tivdesign
